create_provider.note: metadataXml is a proto bytes field — value MUST be base64-encoded. Use metadataUrl (string) as alternative.

oidc_jwt.description: Reusing the same JWT bearer grant assertion is not documented as prevented via jti tracking; ZITADEL documents standard JWT bearer validation fields but no one-time-use enforcement.
oidc_jwt.source: grant-types.mdx and endpoints.mdx JWT Profile Grant sections
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay_same_token or stateless_jwt_no_jti as a vulnerability for JWT bearer grant unless documentation explicitly promises replay prevention.

oidc_jwt.description: userinfo and introspection return claims depending on granted scopes, so missing email/profile/roles claims is by design when scopes were not granted.
oidc_jwt.note: Avoid treating absent optional claims as identity loss or authorization stripping bugs.

oidc_jwt.description: The UserInfo endpoint expects an access token of the user, not a generic client token.
oidc_jwt.note: 401 responses for non-user tokens are expected and should not be treated as authorization regression.

oidc_jwt.description: Token responses may contain scopes that differ from the provided scope parameter, and refresh-token requests may omit scope to reuse the original scope.
oidc_jwt.source: endpoints.mdx token_endpoint authorization code and refresh token sections
oidc_jwt.note: Compare effective granted scope and claims against documented semantics, not strict string equality with the request.

oidc_jwt.description: Certain ZITADEL-specific reserved scopes intentionally enforce organization membership or add audience/claims.
oidc_jwt.note: Extra audience or enforced org restrictions from reserved scopes are by design and should not be mistaken for inconsistent authorization.

oidc_jwt.description: Certain reserved scopes actively change enforcement behavior, such as org membership checks or adding project IDs to audience.
oidc_jwt.note: Login failures or changed audiences under these scopes are by design and should not be flagged as unexpected broker behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange defaults requested_token_type to access token when omitted.
oidc_jwt.note: Receiving an access token without explicitly requesting one is documented default behavior, not silent type escalation.

oidc_jwt.description: Token exchange audience must be a subset of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens.
oidc_jwt.note: Rejection for out-of-subset audience is expected behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: Introspection only reports active=true when the requesting client is part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: Inactive introspection can reflect audience mismatch rather than invalid token.

oidc_jwt.description: Introspection returns active=true only if the token is active and the requesting client is part of the token audience.
oidc_jwt.note: active=false with the wrong client does not mean the token itself is invalid.

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token and future_token tests on login_with_jwt, include a CONTROL JWT bearer grant using a valid assertion with exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and iat={{now_epoch}}. Without a control success case, token rejection cannot be distinguished from broken client authentication, bad audience, or malformed assertion setup.

JWT bearer grant assertions used by login_with_jwt MUST include aud containing ZITADEL's issuing domain, exp as a Unix timestamp, iat as a Unix timestamp, and iss/sub matching the service account userId. The JWT header MUST include kid matching the downloaded keyId. Missing or mismatched kid/iss/sub/aud causes rejection unrelated to the invariant under test.

For I2 freshness tests on login_with_jwt, ZITADEL documents that assertion iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Use this as a hard setup boundary: control assertions should set iat={{now_epoch}}, and stale-assertion tests should move iat beyond {{now_epoch_minus_3600}}. Do not interpret failures from older assertions as exp-only enforcement.

For I1 alg_none and resign_attacker_key tests on login_with_jwt, keep kid present and syntactically valid when possible. ZITADEL identifies the key via the JWT header kid; otherwise failures may be caused by key lookup failure rather than signature-verification behavior.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, subject_token_type MUST use one of ZITADEL's supported identifiers. Access tokens may be JWT or opaque with urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token; id_tokens use urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token. Refresh tokens are explicitly not allowed as subject_token and will fail for by-design reasons.

For I5 token exchange audience tests, requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject and actor tokens. If audience is outside that subset, rejection is by design and not evidence of a bug.

For I5 token exchange scope-escalation tests, requested scope on refresh_token grant or token_exchange must be interpreted relative to prior authorization. ZITADEL documents refresh_token scope must be a subset of the originally requested scope, and token exchange may return scopes differing from the request. Compare exchanged scopes/claims against upstream authorization intent, not merely against the requested scope string.

For I5 token exchange type tests, requested_token_type support is limited. JWT as requested_token_type is only supported for access token as JWT in combination with actor_token; refresh_token requested_token_type is not allowed. Do not treat rejection of unsupported token-type combinations as an authorization-binding failure.

For I3 authorization-code flow coherence tests, redirect_uri on exchange_code_for_token MUST exactly match the redirect_uri used on start_oidc_auth. A mismatch yields invalid_grant by design and must not be interpreted as state/code binding behavior.

For I3 PKCE tests, ZITADEL supports only code_challenge_method=S256. If testing PKCE enforcement, use S256 on the authorization request and vary only presence/value of code_verifier at the token request. Other methods fail for unsupported-method reasons, not for PKCE binding semantics.

For I2 nonce-related OIDC tests, nonce is REQUIRED by ZITADEL for implicit flow and recommended for code flow. When testing code flow, include nonce on start_oidc_auth and validate it in the returned id_token; otherwise missing nonce handling may reflect client-side omission rather than server-side replay protection.

For I3 state-swap tests, state is only recommended, not mandatory. A valid state-binding test MUST send distinct state values in concurrent authorization requests and verify callback correlation; do not infer a vulnerability from flows where the client omitted state.

For I5 reserved-scope tests, ZITADEL-specific scopes actively change authorization semantics. In particular, urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces organization membership, urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} enforces membership plus username suffix, and urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud adds project id to access-token audience. Do not include these scopes in baseline tests unless the invariant specifically targets their behavior.

For I5 metadata-claim tests, requesting scope urn:zitadel:iam:user:metadata causes user metadata values to be returned base64-encoded. Compare decoded semantic values, not raw encoded strings, when evaluating claim propagation or escalation.

For I5 role-claim tests, role-related reserved scopes can cause additional role claims to appear: urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:role:{rolekey} and urn:zitadel:iam:org:projects:roles. If these scopes are requested, extra role claims are by design. Keep them absent in least-privilege baselines unless the test explicitly targets role assertion behavior.

For I1/I5 introspection tests, introspection active=true is only returned when the requesting client is part of the token audience. A false/limited response from introspect_token can be caused by caller-audience mismatch rather than token invalidity. Use a client that is in the token audience for control introspection.

For I2 revocation tests, introspection is the documented way to verify revocation because it checks whether the token is revoked by client or logout. A revoked token may still be locally well-formed as JWT; use introspect_token after revoke_session rather than only local JWT validation.

For I4 identity tests using verify_granted_identity, ZITADEL userinfo sub is the platform subject identifier, not the original JWT bearer assertion sub from login_with_jwt. JWT bearer grant authenticates a service account and returns tokens for that service account; do not expect downstream sub to echo arbitrary attacker-controlled assertion sub values.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT assertion MUST include time claims relative to execution time: use exp={{now_epoch_plus_N}} for control tokens, exp={{now_epoch_minus_N}} for expired tokens, and nbf={{now_epoch_plus_N}} for future-token tests. Without a control login using a valid assertion, LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from broken client authentication or malformed assertion setup.
oidc_jwt.source: ZITADEL token endpoint JWT profile grant docs and claims docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For JWT bearer grant assertions and private_key_jwt client assertions, aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain exactly, and iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. The fuzzer MUST generate assertions with aud set to the issuer base URL and iat near {{now_epoch}}; otherwise failures are expected and are not proof-validation bugs.

For I1 kid_injection and resign_attacker_key tests against login_with_jwt, the JWT assertion MUST be signed with the downloaded private key corresponding to the configured service account or application key, and the JWT header MUST contain kid equal to that keyId. Missing or wrong kid causes expected rejection and must not be misclassified as a deeper verification flaw.

For OIDC authorization-code tests, redirect_uri matching is exact across authorize and token requests. The fuzzer MUST send the identical redirect_uri value to start_oidc_auth and exchange_code_for_token; redirect_uri_mismatch is expected to fail by design and should be asserted via non-200/error outcome, not identity comparison.

For OIDC flow coherence tests, state is only recommended by docs but is the client-side CSRF/session binding signal. The fuzzer MUST include a unique state in start_oidc_auth and verify the callback returns the unmodified same state; otherwise state_swap-style results are uninterpretable.

For OIDC nonce-related I2/I1 tests, nonce is REQUIRED for implicit flow and recommended for code flow. The fuzzer SHOULD include nonce on start_oidc_auth for all OIDC login tests and MUST include it for implicit-flow variants; missing nonce in implicit flow is invalid setup, not a broker vulnerability.

For PKCE tests, ZITADEL supports only code_challenge_method=S256. The fuzzer MUST use S256 when sending PKCE parameters; failures with other methods are by design and not evidence of flow incoherence.

For pkce_skip and related code-flow tests, code_verifier is required only when the authorization request used PKCE. The fuzzer MUST compare exchange outcomes with and without code_verifier under the same PKCE-enabled authorization request and assert rejection via HTTP/error status, not via identity differences.

For token_exchange audience-binding tests, audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from both subject and actor tokens. The fuzzer MUST first obtain subject/actor tokens whose aud claims already contain the target audience; otherwise rejection is expected by policy and does not demonstrate a validation bug.

For token_exchange scope-escalation tests, requested scope may be rejected as invalid_scope when it exceeds what the resource owner granted. The fuzzer MUST treat invalid_scope as the expected secure outcome and only flag a bug if the exchanged token is issued with claims/scopes beyond upstream authorization.
oidc_jwt.source: ZITADEL endpoints.mdx token exchange error response

oidc_jwt.constraint: For token_exchange token-type tests, supported token types are constrained: subject_token_type refresh_token is not allowed; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted; JWT requested_token_type requires subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt only in combination with actor_token. The fuzzer MUST respect this matrix or expected rejections will create false positives.

For introspection-based freshness checks, active=true is only returned when the requesting client is part of the token audience and client authentication succeeds. The fuzzer MUST introspect with the correct client credentials/assertion for the token's audience; active=false or 401 with the wrong client is expected and not evidence of token invalidity.

For revocation tests, revoke_session requires client authentication appropriate to the token's client context. The fuzzer MUST revoke using the same client identity (client_secret_basic or private_key_jwt) that is authorized for the token; otherwise revocation failure is expected and should not be treated as anti-replay weakness.

For UserInfo verification, verify_granted_identity only accepts access tokens of a user, not client-only tokens. The fuzzer MUST NOT call /oidc/v1/userinfo with client_credentials-style or service-account-only tokens unless the flow actually yields a user subject acceptable to UserInfo; 401 in that case is expected and not an authorization bug.

For reserved-scope audience tests, requesting scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud adds that project id to the access-token audience, and urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:zitadel:aud adds the ZITADEL project id. The fuzzer MUST use these scopes when it needs specific audience values in issued tokens; absence of the audience without the scope is by design.

For organization-binding tests, requesting scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces that the user is a member of the selected organization, and unknown organizations fail. The fuzzer MUST treat failures under this scope as expected policy enforcement, not identity confusion.

For org-domain binding tests, requesting scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} enforces both organization membership and that the username is suffixed by the provided domain. The fuzzer MUST account for this extra username/domain restriction when interpreting login failures.

For JWT IdP upstream OIDC/JWT SSO scenarios, ZITADEL's JWT IdP expects the external JWT in a configured HTTP header and explicitly says it is never passed as a URL parameter; the proxy must forward all original query parameters intact to preserve OIDC state. Any test that drops or rewrites query parameters is invalid setup and can falsely appear as I3 flow breakage.

For JWT IdP trust-anchor tests, ZITADEL validates signature using the configured Keys Endpoint, checks iss against configured issuer, and checks token expiry. The fuzzer MUST vary one of these inputs at a time when testing I1/I2; combined mutations make failures ambiguous.

For OIDC SSO provider tests, ZITADEL ensures at least openid scope is always sent to generic OIDC providers, and for Entra ID also ensures User.Read is always sent. The fuzzer MUST not interpret presence of these scopes as scope escalation by the broker; they are documented provider-minimum behavior.

For I2 freshness tests on login_with_jwt, the JWT bearer assertion MUST include exp in the future and iat no older than 1 hour. Use exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}} and iat={{now_epoch}} for the control token. Assertions with iat older than 1h are rejected by design, so a failed attack token without a valid control cannot distinguish freshness enforcement from malformed test setup.

For I1 JWT bearer tests, the assertion aud claim MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain (https://${CUSTOM_DOMAIN}). If aud does not include the issuer domain, rejection is expected and does not prove signature or key validation behavior.

For I1 JWT bearer tests, the JWT header kid MUST identify the configured keyId from the downloaded key JSON. Missing or wrong kid can cause expected lookup failure before signature-trust logic is exercised, so kid-injection tests must vary kid while keeping all other required fields valid.

For I2 replay_same_token against login_with_jwt, do NOT treat successful reuse of the same JWT bearer assertion as a vulnerability unless the docs explicitly promise one-time use. The provided documentation describes stateless JWT bearer validation requirements (signature, issuer, expiry, iat freshness) but no jti tracking or one-time assertion store.

For OIDC authorization-code tests, redirect_uri matching is exact between authorize and token requests and must also match a preregistered redirect URI. A token exchange failure after changing redirect_uri is expected behavior, not an I3 bug.

For OIDC implicit-flow or request sequences that validate id_token replay protections, nonce MUST be supplied on the authorization request. ZITADEL states nonce MUST be provided for implicit flow and returns it in the ID token when provided. Missing nonce makes replay-oriented conclusions invalid.

For OIDC state-swap and flow-coherence tests, state is only recommended, not mandatory. The fuzzer MUST send a unique state on every authorization request and verify the returned state value, otherwise a missing-state setup weakens the test and can create false positives unrelated to ZITADEL behavior.

For PKCE tests, code_challenge_method supports only S256. Do not send plain or alternative methods and interpret rejection as a security success; such rejection is by documented capability limits, not necessarily proof of session binding correctness.

For PKCE skip tests, use the same authorization code flow with code_challenge on /authorize and omit code_verifier only at /token. Because ZITADEL documents PKCE verification by recomputing the challenge from code_verifier, any failure here should be judged by token endpoint status only, not by identity comparisons.

For token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. If the requested audience is outside that subset, rejection is expected by design and must not be reported as a vulnerability oracle failure.

For token exchange tests involving token types, respect ZITADEL's supported token-type matrix: subject_token_type refresh_token is not allowed; requested_token_type defaults to access token if omitted; requested_token_type jwt is only valid for a JWT signed by client and only in combination with actor_token. Unsupported type combinations must not be treated as security rejections.

For token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, compare requested scope against the original authorization because ZITADEL documents that invalid_scope is returned when requested scope exceeds the scope granted by the resource owner. Rejection on expanded scope is expected behavior.

For refresh-token scope tests, any requested scope on refresh_token grant MUST be a subset of the originally requested scope; otherwise rejection is expected. Do not interpret this as inconsistent authorization behavior.

For UserInfo verification, send an access_token of a user, not a client/service token. The docs explicitly say /oidc/v1/userinfo expects the access_token of the user, not the client. Using a machine token from client_credentials or JWT bearer service-account flow can fail by design and should not be used as an I4 oracle.

For introspection-based verification, active=true additionally depends on the requesting client being part of the token audience. A false or limited introspection response can therefore result from client-audience mismatch rather than token invalidity. The fuzzer MUST keep the introspecting client within the token audience when using introspection as an oracle.

For reserved-scope audience tests, ZITADEL adds project IDs to access-token aud via reserved scopes such as urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud and urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:zitadel:aud. Audience-expansion observed after explicitly requesting these scopes is by design and must not be flagged as overbroad authorization.

For organization-binding tests, requesting scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} or urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} intentionally enforces organization membership and may fail if the user is outside that organization. Such failures are setup-dependent and not evidence of token-validation bugs.

For JWT IdP upstream OIDC/JWT SSO tests, the proxy to /idps/jwt MUST forward all original query parameters intact and place the JWT in the configured HTTP header, never in a URL parameter. Missing query parameters breaks OIDC flow state and can mimic I3 failures unrelated to JWT validation.

For JWT IdP tests, if no custom header name is configured, ZITADEL defaults to Authorization as the JWT carrier header. The fuzzer MUST align the injected header with the configured header name; otherwise rejection is expected and does not test proof validation.

For JWT IdP trust-anchor tests, ZITADEL documents validation of signature via Keys Endpoint, issuer match, and expiry. The fuzzer MUST keep issuer, keys endpoint, and header transport consistent when isolating one invariant; e.g., trust-anchor substitution should change the signing trust while preserving a syntactically valid issuer/aud/exp setup, otherwise failures are ambiguous.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API uses REST gateway paths under /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Do NOT use gRPC Connect paths (e.g., 'zitadel.idp.v2.IdentityProviderService/...'). For IdP setup: create_provider creates the IdP, enable_auth_method adds it to the login policy. Both are needed before IdP login works.
